fit: injected beta-caryophyllene-rich pepper seed extract and mouse nociception
assessment: Acute injected extract increased tail-flick reaction latency versus vehicle in six mice per group. An extract and reflex response cannot estimate a culinary effect.

fit: oral standardized seed extract and diabetic rat tail-flick response
assessment: Five rats per group. Longer thermal response latency with extract versus untreated diabetic control. Diabetes model, concentrated extract and reflex endpoint limit transfer.

fit: piperine-containing blend and exercise with mixed pain findings
assessment: The combination group reported a brief early worsening. Mean NRS was lower at day 14 and zero in both arms at day 30. Exercise, other ingredients and inconsistencies limit attribution.

fit: black-pepper fruit in a four-plant arthritis trial
assessment: Final joint pain VAS difference 3.00 mm (95% CI −1.82 to 7.84); the full noninferiority analysis and arm-level table remain unavailable.

fit: dried multiherb blend and massage in chronic low-back pain
assessment: The combination arm had a lower day-seven NRS than either component arm. Many ingredient exposures and no pepper-only comparison. Daily-dose reporting conflicts.

fit: isolated piperine and distinct thermal and mechanical outcomes in mice
assessment: Thermal response latency was higher in all piperine groups. Mechanical withdrawal threshold was higher only in the two higher-dose groups, with an inconclusive low-dose test. No clinical outcome.

fit: three-extract formula and knee osteoarthritis pain versus naproxen
assessment: The original Persian Table 2 gives week-four VAS 4.53 versus 4.37 and inconclusive group p=.747. Both arms changed over time. Likely companion cohort to the separate English PGE2 report. No cracked pepper or Parkinson sample.

fit: piperine-containing add-on formulation in an open clinical comparison
assessment: All groups received dexibuprofen. Pain ratings favored a curcumin, lipoic acid and piperine combination. Neither the piperine effect nor an effect of culinary pepper in Parkinson disease is isolated.

fit: registered curcumin and piperine blend with stent-symptom outcome
assessment: Official record lists nine actual enrollees and a secondary stent-symptom questionnaire. No results posted. Single arm, multiple ingredients, no Parkinson group.
